coverage: The fixture reads ID_NAME, ID_DEVIDS, PROP_BITS, EV_BITS, and ABS_INFO through the virtio-mmio config window and compares the exact little-endian payload bytes.
Unsupported EV_BITS, unknown selectors, maximum subselectors, and reads beyond the 136-byte config surface return zero without leaking a previous union payload.
A width-2 selector write updates select/subsel byte-for-byte, and reset returns the selector state to UNSET.
InputDeviceSpec bounds property/event bit and ABS-axis setters to fixed host-owned arrays; the new device advertises virtio id 18 and two queues.

virtio_regression.command: cargo test -p wasm-vm-core --test virtio_mmio_slots --test virtio_blk --test virtio_net_critic --quiet

runner.coverage: The wasm32 runner compares the same name, devids, property, event-bitmap, and ABS_INFO fixture bytes and zero-payload behavior.

claim: At commit ea342ce, VirtioInput provides a bounded, little-endian virtio-input configuration state machine built from InputDeviceSpec, with exact ID/devids/bitmap/ABS payloads, zeroed unsupported queries, device id 18, and native/wasm32 parity.
scope_notes: Eventq/statusq transport and host injection are intentionally deferred to E5-T10b and E5-T10c.
No independent-machine, WebKit, or host-layer rr run was used, per the user's direction and the repository's current evidence policy.
